todos.note: learn-from-the-test.md's own 'Meta (trainer) > Delivery architecture' bullet describes the packaged re-send as running 'in a fresh session there (cross-cwd boundary, so `new`, not the same session as diagnose + build + assemble)'. Read against the actual mechanics (`exercises/fork-the-worktree.md` Session widget: fork runs in the ORIGINAL repo; `exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` Session widget: diagnose+build+assemble opens 'Session (new, "Module 5 worktree session")' already IN the worktree; Phase 5's re-send is 'Session (new, "M5 long-run")', also in the worktree — same cwd as diagnose+build+assemble, just a fresh session for a clean context window per L109-117 of that exercise), the actual cross-cwd boundary is the earlier fork step (original repo -> worktree), not the diagnose-to-resend step, which is same-cwd/new-session. This is trainer-only Meta text, not student body — the student-facing Session widgets in both exercises are unambiguous and independently verified PASS on rule 4 — so it is not a cross_module violation, but it misdescribes the boundary for a trainer reading the Meta note and is worth a correction pass. Also worth reconciling: check_cross_module.md §4's own canonical-case line ('M5 opens new in `../<repo>-m5` worktree') compresses M5's actual two-step open (original repo for the fork, then the worktree for diagnose+build+assemble+resend) into one clause; not a file defect, just a coarser compendium description than the current file architecture.
